notes: The phrase about the direction of their faces is difficult; “eastward” preserves the directional term without resolving the whole image.
“We will not die” follows the pinned Hebrew wording. The prophet’s appeal holds this confidence beside the violence he questions.
vocabulary: The people associated here with the advancing Babylonian power.
A large fishing net; people are pictured as a conqueror’s catch.

notes: “Faithfulness” can also be rendered “faith.” The Hebrew describes the righteous person’s faithful trust; the swollen or puffed-up person stands in contrast.
The pinned Hebrew reads “wine.” The difficult opening is not silently changed to “wealth.”
The drink image joins intoxication, exposure, and judgment. The term rendered “fury” can also suggest venom or poison; the command about uncircumcision follows the written wording.
“Them” retains the Hebrew pronoun referring back to the animals rather than changing it to “you.”
vocabulary: A received prophetic revelation, here to be written and awaited.
The LORD’s sacred dwelling, before which the earth is summoned to silence.

notes: “Shigionoth” and “Selah” are retained as ancient performance or musical terms whose precise force is uncertain.
“Oaths, rods, a word” represents an exceptionally difficult Hebrew phrase. Its syntax and relation to the bow image remain uncertain; the draft does not claim to resolve it.
The Hebrew moves from a house’s foundation to a neck. The mixed image is preserved rather than reconstructed as a single clear scene.
The final clause about the attacking people is difficult. The draft preserves waiting and distress without fixing an otherwise unstated timetable.
vocabulary: Southern place names within the poem’s depiction of God’s approach.
The heights in the deer-footed movement image; not necessarily worship sites here.
